html:
SMTO-CFG-0003 — One of SMTO's prompts has a formatting problem

GUID: 1fd0f7a7-3ba3-4cdb-8c48-943936c3f0ce
Slug: prompt-template-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO fills in blanks in its prompts (the instructions it sends to the model) before using them. One prompt is empty, has a stray dollar sign, or asks for a blank SMTO can't fill.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Agent behavior › Prompts, select Open Prompt Editor, and set the status filter to Customized. Built-in prompts are checked before they ship, so a problem like this comes from a prompt that was edited.
  2. In each customized prompt, look for a lone dollar sign and type two dollar signs instead. Make sure the prompt isn't empty, then select Save. SMTO reads a single dollar sign as the start of a blank to fill in, so an ordinary price written that way breaks the prompt.
  3. On the Rendered preview tab, select Render preview to test the prompt. If you're unsure what to fix, select Restore this prompt to go back to the shipped wording. The preview shows the same problem SMTO hit, and restoring removes the edit that caused it.

What success looks like

  • Render preview shows the finished text, and your next request runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • If no prompts are customized, select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't select Restore all prompts unless you're happy to lose every prompt edit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A prompt template could not be rendered: the body is blank, contains invalid string.Template dollar-placeholder syntax, or references a placeholder variable that was not supplied.

What this means

  • A prompt template is blank, has invalid string.Template placeholder syntax or references a substitution value that was not supplied. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • A prompt template is blank, has invalid string.Template placeholder syntax or references a substitution value that was not supplied.

How to diagnose it

  • Check placeholder syntax and required variable names against the owning template's rendering inputs, without exposing private values.

How to fix it

  • Identify the prompt key from Technical details, then in Prompt Editor fix the body (escape a literal dollar sign as $$, use only the placeholder names the shipped default declares, and keep the body non-empty) or restore the shipped default. For a legacy stored helper template, correct or remove its record in the user prompts store.
  • Correct the template or supply its required render variables through the owning configuration; use the matching built-in template when appropriate.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended template renders successfully with its actual required variables.

What not to do
